title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In these 1983-84 notes on surgery of conformal surfaces, the previous page sets up two triangles of moduli 'multiplicities' (stacks). Case 1: MDB_{g,ν} → M_st ND_{g,ν}, both mapping to mdt_{g,ν}. Here the marked points are replaced by boundary discs, or carry 'toric' (circle) structures, and the real dimension is that of C^{3g-3+ν}×R^ν. Case 2: MD_{g,ν} → M_st N_{g,ν} over md_{g,ν}, a diagram of C-algebraic multiplicities of complex dimension 3g-3+ν. The left-hand objects are moduli of surfaces equipped with systems of discs (a 'Mumford–Deligne'-type moduli of stable curves seen through disc structures, MD). The right-hand objects are moduli of stable/nodal curves. Page 79 ends with these arrows; R^ν matches, for example, the ν boundary lengths of bordered hyperbolic surfaces (6g-6+3ν real parameters).

This page (numbered 13) asks two questions. Are these arrows isomorphisms? If so, how do we write down an explicit inverse?

First answer, conditional. Suppose the conjectural determination of an 'admissible system of discs' on a compact holomorphic surface, via the hyperbolic-type function/metric, were correct. Then the inverse arrows would be immediate: hyperbolic geometry would canonically select the discs.

Second answer, at the naive level of functors between fibred categories, by plumbing. Take a nodal curve whose normalization X' has the node branches at x_i' and x_i''. The smoothing datum is a nonzero u_i in T*_{x_i'} ⊗ T*_{x_i''}. Grothendieck writes ∧, but for lines the tensor product is meant. Equivalently, its inverse is a nonzero element of the dual line T_{x_i'} ⊗ T_{x_i''}, that is, a perfect pairing T_{x_i'} ⊗ T_{x_i''} → C, or an isomorphism T_{x_i''} ≅ T_{x_i'}^∨. This is exactly the standard fact that the normal direction to the boundary divisor at a node is T_{x'} ⊗ T_{x''}, with local equation zw = t.

The gluing then proceeds in four steps:
- Choose a round (conformal) disc D_i' in the tangent line T_{x_i'}.
- The pairing turns z ↦ 1/z into the inversion, which sends the complement of D_i' to a 'full' disc D_i'' in T_{x_i''}.
- Transport neighbourhoods of these discs into the surface X' (next page). This gives identifications between neighbourhoods of the boundary circles of D_i' and D_i''.
- Remove the open discs and glue to get a smooth surface X, possibly with boundary if discs around the marked points x_α are also removed.

The glued circles Γ_i need not be geodesics. By Thurston's principles, each is freely homotopic to a unique closed geodesic, which gives canonical curves. Grothendieck flags (next page) that independence of the result from the choice of the pairs (D_i', D_i'') is open, with only a 'vaseux' (muddy) heuristic argument.

The purpose is to identify the moduli of surfaces with disc/boundary structures with (a real-oriented blow-up of) the Deligne–Mumford compactification. In effect this gives plumbing coordinates near the boundary, and asks whether hyperbolic geometry makes them canonical.
errors: Writing u_i ∈ T*_{x'} ∧_C T*_{x''} should be a tensor product of the two cotangent lines; a wedge of two distinct lines makes no sense here. This is notational only.

Plumbing with chosen discs and coordinates is not canonical. The resulting point of moduli depends on the choices beyond first order, so it gives an inverse only as a germ or up to homotopy, not literally an inverse isomorphism. Grothendieck himself flags this as unresolved, with only a heuristic argument.
The whole construction is conditional on the 'conjectural determination' of admissible disc systems by the hyperbolic metric; it is not proved on this page.

ideas.what: Smoothing parameter of a node lives in T*_{x'}⊗T*_{x''} (dually T_{x'}⊗T_{x''}); a nonzero element gives a pairing identifying T_{x''} with the dual of T_{x'}
ideas.modern_name: normal bundle to the boundary divisor of M̄_{g,n} is T_{x'}⊗T_{x''} (−ψ'−ψ'')
ideas.where_published: Not explicitly; Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Mumford–Deligne compactification and the Teichmüller tower only qualitatively

ideas.what: Gluing nodal curves by choosing a disc in one tangent line and its inversion-complement in the other, then removing discs and identifying collars
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kra, Maskit, Earle–Marden, Masur (1970s), Fay 1973, Wolpert

ideas.what: Canonical determination of a system of 'admissible discs' on a Riemann surface by the hyperbolic metric, with glued circles replaced by unique geodesic representatives (Thurston)
ideas.modern_name: hyperbolic collars / Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates; canonical plumbing via hyperbolic geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bers, Thurston, Wolpert (plumbing vs. hyperbolic degeneration, 1990s–2000s)

ideas.what: Moduli of surfaces with disc/boundary ('discoidal') structures compared with moduli of stable curves with toric (circle) structures at marked points, with real dimension 6g-6+3ν
ideas.modern_name: real-oriented blow-up of M̄_{g,n} (Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov, Looijenga); moduli of bordered surfaces / framed little-disc modular operad

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether the comparison maps between moduli of conformal surfaces with disc systems and moduli of stable curves (with toric structures) are isomorphisms. He proposes to invert them canonically using a conjectural hyperbolically determined system of admissible discs, and leaves independence of choices open.
missed.quote: Question Les flèches sont-elles des iso — et si oui, comment expliciter un iso en sens inverse?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Canonical (choice-free) plumbing coordinates matching the DM boundary with hyperbolic/real-blow-up structures matter for string field theory vertices (hyperbolic string vertices, Costello–Zwiebach 2019) and for modular operads of framed surfaces. This 1983-84 formulation predates those and Segal's disc-gluing axioms.

missed.claim: Implicit link between Teichmüller-tower 'surgery' (Esquisse) and what later became gluing of Riemann surfaces along parametrized discs (Segal CFT, framed little discs). Using hyperbolic geodesics to make the gluing canonical anticipates hyperbolic string vertices.
missed.quote: choisissant un disque conforme D_i' dans T_{x_i'}, d'où disque conforme plein D_i'' dans T_{x_i''}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: an early, independent articulation of disc-gluing moduli in Grothendieck's program. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard plumbing, and the normal-bundle description of the boundary divisor is classical. The notable part is Grothendieck's (1983-84) aim to make plumbing canonical via hyperbolic geometry, and to compare disc-structured moduli with real-blown-up DM moduli. This anticipates later work (Segal, KSV, hyperbolic string vertices) but remains conjectural and heuristic here.
transcription_corrections: 'Si la déformation conjecturale' should read 'Si la détermination conjecturale'.
'par[?] la fonction de type hyperbolique' should read '(par la fonction de type hyperbolique)', with 'surface holomorphe compacte'.
'on dominait[?]' is likely 'on trouverait' (or 'on construirait') des flèches.
'u_i ∈ T*_{x_i'} ∧_C T*_{x_i''}': the ∧ should be read as ⊗; 'on a quel venant au' is likely 'ou ce qui revient au même un'.
'T_{x_i} ⊗ T_{x_i''} → C' should read 'T_{x_i'} ⊗ T_{x_i''} → C'.
'Ex[?]' at the end of line 3 appears to be a crossed-out abbreviation, possibly 'Est'.
